_about: Every number the manuscript states, paired with the report file and the
exact location inside it that produces the number. check_expected.py
reads this file, reads the reports a run produced, and prints a table of
agreements and disagreements.
On 'the manuscript'. There are two: paper/paper_main.tex, the six-page
IEEEtran submission, and paper/paper_long.tex, a twelve-page single-column
variant kept as a source of material. A number printed in either one is
checked here. The six-page version summarises the input-resolution study
and points to this artefact for it, so several grid and gap checks guard
numbers only the twelve-page version prints; they still have to agree.
On tolerances. Each entry carries its own 'tol' and a one-line reason.
Counts and parameter counts are exact: a mismatch there is a different
dataset or a different model, not noise. Trained quantities are not
exact and are not claimed to be. Training is stochastic, cuDNN kernel
selection is not deterministic across GPU models, and the manuscript
reports between-seed standard deviations as high as 0.16 on some cells of
the grid. The tolerance on a trained quantity is therefore set from the
reported spread of that quantity, not from a wish for a tight match. An
entry whose tolerance looks generous is one the manuscript already
describes as noisy, and the manuscript's own claim about it is
correspondingly weak.
What a pass means: the run reproduced the number inside the spread the
paper reports for it. What a failure means: look at it. A failure on an
exact count means the archive differs. A failure on a trained quantity
outside its stated spread means the conclusion drawn from it does not
hold on this machine, and that is worth knowing and worth reporting.
